title: [7/1/2023] Reasons for university choice
prompt: The pie chart below shows the main reasons why students chose to study at a particular UK university in 1997 and 2007. Summarize the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The pie charts compare five major factors that influenced students' decisions when choosing a UK university in 1997 and 2007.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, while some reasons such as proximity to parental home became more important over the decade, others like sports and social activities declined significantly in relevance. Throughout both years, suitable degree courses remained the most commonly cited factor.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Starting with the reasons that grew in importance, suitable degree courses was the dominant factor in both years, accounting for 35% of responses in 1997 before rising slightly to 37% a decade later. Meanwhile, proximity to parental home saw the most dramatic increase, more than doubling from 10% to 22% over the period. Quality of teaching also experienced a modest rise, climbing from 15% to 18%, making it the third most popular reason by 2007.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: As for the declining factors, the proportion of students who chose universities based on good sports and social activities fell sharply from 19% in 1997 to just 6% in 2007, representing the most significant decrease among all categories. Similarly, quality of resource, which was the second most important factor in 1997 at 21%, dropped to 17% over the same period, becoming less influential than proximity to home.
